title: Almost Home
style: new-age synth-pop, nocturnal and introspective, steady midtempo pulse with rounded sequenced bass and glassy analog pads; begin with a close, breath-soft mezzo-soprano over sparse piano and distant bell tones, add crisp restrained electronic percussion and warm low synth through the verses, open into a wide melodic chorus with subtle wordless backing harmonies, then strip back to piano and voice for a reflective bridge before a final fuller chorus; polished spacious mix, clear intimate lead vocal
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The ferry clock forgets to move
Blue water holds the harbor still
Your paper cup goes cold between us
A gull turns once above the hill

[Pre-Chorus]
You say the morning has a name
I say it changes when we do
The windows keep our borrowed faces
And every road leads back to you

[Chorus]
Let it stay sweet, this almost-home
Tallinn standing still beneath our feet
Eyes from the dance floor, soft and far
I thought we were home, wherever we are
Let it stay sweet, don't make it true
One quiet night with a view of you

[Verse 2]
We missed the turn by Viru Square
The rain made silver of the signs
You laughed and tucked your hair away
As if we had all the time

[Pre-Chorus]
No grand confession, no escape
Just footsteps finding their own pace
The city kept its windows open
And held the weather in its face

[Chorus]
Let it stay sweet, this almost-home
Tallinn standing still beneath our feet
Eyes from the dance floor, soft and far
I thought we were home, wherever we are
Let it stay sweet, don't make it true
One quiet night with a view of you

[Bridge]
If this is only borrowed shelter
Let the walls remember rain
Let the door remain unlatched
Let us leave without a name

[Final Chorus]
Let it stay sweet, this almost-home
Tallinn standing still beneath our feet
Eyes from the dance floor, soft and far
I thought we were home, wherever we are
Let it stay sweet, the dawn can wait
Your hand in mine beside the gate
One quiet night, a little room
A tender place that won't stay true

[Outro]
The ferry clock begins again
You turn; the harbor keeps the blue
